evals.prompt: Scaffold a new Python MCP server. What transport should it use and how should logging be wired?
expected_behaviors: Serves over Streamable HTTP via streamable_http_app() behind Uvicorn, not stdio unless explicitly required.
Directs all logging to stderr with a single root StreamHandler and a JSON formatter; no per-module handlers.
Obtains loggers with logging.getLogger(__name__), never hardcoded names or vendored logger objects.
Loads logging config at the entrypoint import time and passes log_config= to uvicorn.run.
Caps third-party HTTP client loggers (httpx, httpcore) at WARNING in logging.conf.
failure_signals: Defaults to stdio transport without a stated requirement.
Logs to stdout or creates per-module handlers.
Uses a hardcoded logger name or a shared logger object from a config loader.
Loads logging config only in the parent launcher, breaking under reload=True.
Leaves httpx/httpcore at INFO, producing per-request noise.

evals.prompt: Add a new tool to this MCP server that fetches data from an external API. Describe the layers the call passes through and where each piece of code lives.
expected_behaviors: Follows the dependency direction: MCP tool -> application use case -> domain Protocol -> infrastructure adapter -> external API.
Keeps domain code framework-free (no mcp/httpx imports in domain).
Registers the tool explicitly in infra/tools/registry.py with no automatic module discovery.
Loads configuration through Pydantic BaseSettings + python-dotenv at the composition boundary, not inside business logic.
Places the external API client in infra/adapters/ behind a domain interface.
failure_signals: Calls the external API directly from the tool function, skipping the use case and adapter.
Imports httpx or the mcp SDK inside domain code.
Relies on automatic tool discovery instead of explicit registration.
Reads environment variables inside business logic.
Reverses the dependency direction (domain importing infra).

evals.prompt: A tool needs to include a request correlation ID in its log lines for traceability. How is this done in this skeleton?
expected_behaviors: Declares ctx: Context (from mcp.server.mcpserver.context) on the tool.
Passes extra={"request_id": ctx.request_id} on log calls.
Notes the formatter includes request_id only when present.
Does NOT use ctx.log()/ctx.info() or the MCP logging capability (deprecated, SEP-2577).
Keeps logging server-side on stderr.
failure_signals: Uses the deprecated ctx.log()/ctx.info() MCP logging capability.
Generates a random correlation ID instead of using ctx.request_id.
Omits the Context parameter and cannot correlate logs.
Logs over the protocol to the client instead of server-side stderr.
Hardcodes the request_id into the logger rather than passing it per call.

evals.prompt: How do I manually verify this MCP server works using MCP Inspector or curl? Walk me through it.
expected_behaviors: Explains the Streamable HTTP session handshake: initialize returns an mcp-session-id header that must be sent on every subsequent request.
Sends notifications/initialized before any tools/call.
Sequences the flow: initialize -> notifications/initialized -> tools/call.
On PowerShell, writes JSON request bodies to temp files and uses curl.exe --data-binary "@file" to avoid inline-JSON mangling.
Verifies via the test suite and a live boot before declaring success.
failure_signals: Calls tools/call without initialize and the session handshake.
Omits the mcp-session-id header on subsequent requests.
Skips notifications/initialized before tools/call.
Pipes inline JSON through PowerShell curl and hits quoting errors without the temp-file workaround.
Claims it works based only on code inspection without running it.

evals.prompt: A tool returns data containing non-ASCII characters (e.g. 'Flabébé') and the server crashes on Windows with a UnicodeEncodeError when logging. What is the cause and fix?
expected_behaviors: Identifies that Windows stderr is often cp1252 and cannot encode some non-ASCII characters.
Keeps json.dumps default ensure_ascii=True in the formatter so non-ASCII data is escaped.
Explains this prevents UnicodeEncodeError regardless of the console code page.
Verifies the fix by logging a non-ASCII value without error.
Does not 'fix' it by switching stdout encoding in a way that breaks the protocol.
failure_signals: Blames the data source instead of the console encoding.
Sets ensure_ascii=False, making the crash worse on cp1252.
Cannot connect the UnicodeEncodeError to the Windows stderr code page.
Suggests stripping non-ASCII characters from the data.
Proposes a fix that writes logs to stdout and corrupts the protocol.
